subject: general
question: What is the term for India’s mainstream Hindi-language film industry?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bollywood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bollywood refers to the mainstream Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, India.
 
• It is one of the largest centers of film production in the world, producing hundreds of films annually.
 
• The term "Bollywood" is a blend of "Bombay" (former name of Mumbai) and "Hollywood," signifying its prominence in the global film industry.
 
• Bollywood films are known for their elaborate song-and-dance sequences, dramatic storytelling, and diverse genres.
 
• It has a massive global audience, with Indian expatriates and international viewers enjoying Bollywood movies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tollywood**

 
 
• Tollywood refers to the Telugu-language film industry based in Hyderabad, Telangana.
 
• It is one of the major regional film industries in India and is known for producing films with high-budget action sequences and compelling storytelling.
 
• Films like "Baahubali" and "RRR" have gained international acclaim and spotlighted Tollywood on the global stage.
 
 
 
• **Kollywood**
 
 
• Kollywood represents the Tamil-language film industry based in Chennai, Tamil Nadu.
 
• Renowned for its artistic and socially relevant films, Kollywood has a rich history in Indian cinema.
 
• It is home to legendary filmmakers and actors like Mani Ratnam, Rajinikanth, and Kamal Haasan.
 
 
 
• **Mollywood**
 
 
• Mollywood refers to the Malayalam-language film industry based in Kerala.
 
• Known for its realistic storytelling and high-quality content, Mollywood has produced critically acclaimed films like "Drishyam" and "Bangalore Days."
 
• It has a reputation for addressing socially relevant themes and showcasing cultural diversity.
